html:
A Chinese philosopher of the Southern Song dynasty who pulled together the ideas known as Neo-Confucianism. His reading of the classics became official teaching in China, Korea and Japan for some six hundred years.

Building on earlier thinkers, he taught that everything has a principle (li) that gives it its pattern, and a material force (qi) that makes it real. People become good by investigating things and studying the classics until they grasp principle. This gave Confucian ethics a full account of the universe, able to stand against Buddhism and Daoism.

He chose four short texts, the Four Books, as the core of learning: the Analects of Confucius, the Mencius, the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean. He wrote commentaries on all of them.

In 1313 the Yuan made his commentaries the standard for the imperial examinations, and so they stayed until 1905. Joseon Korea took his school as its state ideology, through scholars like Yi Hwang, and Tokugawa Japan honoured it too.
sum: A Chinese philosopher of the Southern Song dynasty who pulled together the ideas known as Neo-Confucianism. His reading of the classics became official teaching in China, Korea and Japan for some six hundred years.
